use_case: Tenant screening recommendations: the property management platform's integrated screening service scores each rental application and returns accept, accept with conditions (higher deposit), or decline with reason codes; about 15,500 applications a year
vendor_or_model: Tenant screening provider integrated in the property management platform (vendor scoring model on consumer report, eviction, criminal record, and income data; company-set thresholds)
data_categories: Applicant identity data and Social Security numbers; consumer reports (credit, eviction filings, criminal records); income and employment; housing voucher status
human_in_the_loop: Today the recommendation is the decision in practice (override rate 2.1%). Required from 2026-10-31: a leasing coordinator reviews every decline and conditional approval against published written criteria, with individualized review of criminal and eviction records, before any notice
applicable_laws: Fair Housing Act 42 U.S.C. 3604(a), (b), (f); 24 CFR 100.500 (in force; HUD proposed changes 2026); Fla. Stat. 760.23; FCRA 15 U.S.C. 1681b and 1681m(a); FCRA disposal rule 16 CFR 682.3; N53-R02 FTC Act Section 5 (45(a)); service provider oversight under N53-R01 (314.4(f)) applied by company choice

use_case: Buyer lead scoring: the CRM scores inbound buyer inquiries (A, B, C) and sets the order in which inside sales agents respond; about 6,500 leads a month; A and B leads are offered a referral to the mortgage joint venture after consent
business_owner: Director of Inside Sales and Relocation
vendor_or_model: CRM vendor lead scoring feature (vendor machine learning model configured by the company)
data_categories: Inquiry contact data; ZIP code; inquiry language; price range; pre-approval status; web activity
human_in_the_loop: Inside sales agents see the score and choose whom to call; policy requires a same-day response to every lead, which the scoring currently undermines
applicable_laws: Fair Housing Act 42 U.S.C. 3604(b), (d); Fla. Stat. 760.23; RESPA 12 CFR 1024.15(b) for joint venture referrals; N53-R02 FTC Act Section 5 (45(a))
status: In production; ZIP code and language inputs to be removed by 2026-11-30

use_case: Generative AI assistant for marketing: drafts listing descriptions, social posts, and agent marketing copy
vendor_or_model: Enterprise generative AI assistant with no-training contract terms (pilot since 2026-07); public chatbots used informally before the pilot
data_categories: Property features and marketing copy; risk of client, tenant, or applicant data being pasted
risk_tier: Low (High if client data is entered or if it is used to target or exclude audiences)
human_in_the_loop: Marketing staff or the listing agent edits every draft and checks it for discriminatory statements before publication
applicable_laws: Fair Housing Act 42 U.S.C. 3604(c) (discriminatory advertising); N53-R01 (314.4(c)(1)(ii)) and POL-05 4.8 for client data; N53-R02 FTC Act Section 5 (45(a))
status: Enterprise tool approved with conditions; public tools blocked on company devices by 2026-12-31 (P01 R-043)

use_case: Leasing assistant chatbot on the leasing website: answers prospects' questions about available rentals, schedules showings, and collects pre-screening information
vendor_or_model: Chatbot vendor (large language model with a scripted knowledge base of listings and policies)
data_categories: Prospect names, phone numbers, email addresses, move-in dates, household size, pets and assistance animals (free text)
human_in_the_loop: Showings are confirmed by a leasing agent; questions about eligibility, accommodations, or assistance animals must hand off to a leasing agent; no applications are decided by the chatbot
applicable_laws: Fair Housing Act 42 U.S.C. 3604(c) and (f), including reasonable accommodations (3604(f)(3)(B)); Fla. Stat. 760.23; N53-R02 FTC Act Section 5 (45(a)); disclosure of AI interaction (company rule)
status: In production since 2026-03; fair housing fixes and AI disclosure due 2026-12-31

use_case: Identity verification for closings: document authentication, selfie face match, and database checks for remote buyers and sellers before Title and Closing accepts signed documents or disburses proceeds; about 3,100 checks a year
vendor_or_model: Identity verification vendor (document analysis and face-matching models), integrated with the e-signature service
data_categories: Government ID images; selfie images and face-match scores (biometric data); name, address, and date of birth
consequential_decision_category: Financial (release of sale proceeds); housing transaction
human_in_the_loop: A closer reviews every failed check and every pass on a high-risk file (vacant land, non-owner-occupied, recently changed contact data) and decides whether to require a known-notary signing; the tool never blocks a closing on its own
applicable_laws: N53-R01 (314.4(c)(1)(i), (f)); Fla. Stat. 501.171 (biometric data is personal information under 501.171(1)(g)1.a.(VI)); Fla. Stat. 626.8473(4) (disburse only per instructions); N53-R02 FTC Act Section 5 (45(a))
status: In production since 2025-10; threshold tuning and vendor data terms due 2026-12-31
